summary: Frontend-only smoke test of new pseudo-3D canvas upgrade at /app (Angular 21 SSR) on preview URL. Navigated through splash-onboarding → GUEST auth → start-sprint-btn → in-game orientation skip → gameplay. CRITICAL FINDING: The in-game runner canvas renders as completely empty/transparent — no perspective floor, no player, no obstacles, no shadows visible. Instrumentation confirms the gameLoop IS running (requestAnimationFrame ticking at ~75 fps, 30 000+ fillRect calls per second) so draw() is executing — yet CanvasRenderingContext2D.getImageData() returns [0,0,0,0] (fully transparent) for every sampled pixel (corners, center, bottom), AND a direct element.screenshot of the #gameCanvas node shows a pure-black frame. Strongly suggests the `this.ctx` held by the component is bound to a stale/detached <canvas> (likely the SSR-rendered one before hydration) while the live DOM canvas the user sees is a different element that never receives paint commands. The pseudo-3D blocks (perspective floor at L4927-4988, player cast shadow at L5027-5048, obstacle cast shadow + depth-scale at L5273-5327) are syntactically sound in code review but cannot be visually verified because NOTHING is rendering. No JS pageerrors or uncaught exceptions — only a benign Firestore-offline warning (expected in this env).

ui_bugs.issue: Canvas renders completely black/empty during gameState==='playing'. getImageData on every sampled coord returns [0,0,0,0] transparent despite gameLoop firing ~75 fps and draw() issuing 30k+ fillRect calls/sec. Pseudo-3D perspective floor, player & obstacle cast shadows, depth-scale — NONE are visually present because the canvas backing store is empty. Likely cause: `this.ctx = this.canvasRef.nativeElement.getContext('2d')` is captured inside afterNextRender() BEFORE Angular hydration swaps the SSR <canvas> element for the CSR one, so all subsequent draw calls target a detached/orphaned canvas while the on-screen canvas never receives paint. Fix direction: move ctx acquisition to an AfterViewInit-equivalent that runs post-hydration, or lazily re-acquire ctx whenever canvasRef.nativeElement differs from the one ctx was taken from.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot verify pseudo-3D floor / player shadow / obstacle shadow / depth-scale — entire canvas is blank. Feature ships visually broken even though the code paths are exercised.

issues: HUD + keyboard-shortcut chips (SPC/E/F/C) render correctly above the canvas — no layout issue there; purely a canvas-paint issue.

action_items: HIGHEST PRIORITY — Fix the orphaned-ctx bug. Suggest adding an `ngAfterViewInit()` (or a safer `afterNextRender` that runs on every stable view re-check) that re-executes `this.ctx = this.canvasRef.nativeElement.getContext('2d')` whenever `this.canvasRef.nativeElement` !== the element previously captured. A one-liner diagnostic: inside draw() assert `this.ctx.canvas.isConnected === true` and log once if false — that will immediately confirm the detached-canvas hypothesis.

Re-verify pseudo-3D perspective floor + cast shadows + depth-scale ONLY after the canvas paint bug is fixed. Code at app.ts lines 4927-4988 (floor), 5027-5048 (player shadow), 5273-5327 (obstacle shadow + depth scale) looks correct.

Watercooler reply smoke-test was NOT executed because I stayed inside the game loop trying to diagnose the canvas regression. Given the canvas is visually broken, watercooler should be re-tested after the canvas fix in the next iteration.

Minor: console warning 'Canvas2D: Multiple readback operations using getImageData are faster with the willReadFrequently attribute set to true' — not a bug, but if there is any in-app getImageData path in draw() consider setting willReadFrequently:true.
critical_code_review_comments: app.ts is 5648 lines — far above the 700-line guideline. Split the runner-game logic (draw, update, gameLoop, spawn* methods) into a dedicated service or component; the main AppComponent is carrying UI shell + game engine + auth wiring + quest system.

`afterNextRender` is used for the one-shot `this.ctx = ... ; this.gameLoop();` initialisation. This fires once BEFORE full browser hydration in SSR apps. That's the most likely root cause of the black-canvas bug — the ctx captured refers to the pre-hydration canvas instance.

Inside draw() the first op is `this.ctx.save()`; if `this.ctx` is null/stale every call becomes a no-op silently (no throw because the method still exists on the orphan). Adding `if (!this.ctx?.canvas?.isConnected) return;` + a single console.warn would make this class of bug self-diagnosing.

canvasRef is accessed in many places (lines 3870, 3872, 4285, 4442, 4452, 4561, 4715 …). Centralise into a getter that also validates `isConnected` to prevent divergence between the rendered DOM canvas and the captured ctx.

test_credentials: Guest mode only (Firebase Anonymous Auth). No email creds needed — two consent checkboxes + ENTER AS GUEST.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro: 1) viewport 1280x900 (or mobile 390x844 — reproduces on both). 2) goto preview URL, wait 3.5 s, click NEXT 3× to clear splash. 3) GUEST tab → tick 2-3 checkboxes → ENTER AS GUEST (waits ~3.5s for anonymous auth). 4) Click [data-testid='start-sprint-btn']. 5) In-game 'Employee Orientation' panel appears — click its Skip button. 6) Canvas area will be visible but BLACK. Confirm via JS: `const c=document.querySelector('canvas'); const d=c.getContext('2d').getImageData(700,250,1,1).data; // returns [0,0,0,0]`. Simultaneously `window._rafCount` (after monkey-patching RAF) and `window._fillRectCount` (after monkey-patching CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.fillRect) increase every frame, proving gameLoop is live — the paints just go to a detached canvas. PSEUDO-3D CODE ITSELF LOOKS CORRECT — the bug blocking verification is a ctx-acquisition / hydration timing issue, not the new rendering code.
rca of the issue: Root cause (high confidence): In AppComponent.constructor(), `afterNextRender(() => { this.ctx = this.canvasRef.nativeElement.getContext('2d'); this.gameLoop(); })` runs once, at the first post-render tick. With Angular 21 SSR, the DOM <canvas> present at that moment is the server-rendered node, which is later replaced (or detached) during client hydration of the surrounding @if / bindings. `this.ctx` retains a reference to the OLD canvas's 2D context, so all draw/fillRect ops paint into an orphaned off-DOM canvas. The live on-screen <canvas> the user sees never gets painted — hence black screen and getImageData = [0,0,0,0]. `window._fillRectCount` still climbs because the ops do execute, just on the wrong canvas. Mitigation: (a) move ctx capture to ngAfterViewInit OR (b) wrap canvasRef access in a getter that re-calls getContext when `this._lastCanvas !== this.canvasRef.nativeElement`, OR (c) set `canvasRef` via a `@ViewChild('gameCanvas', { static: false })` + re-bind whenever the view checks. After the fix, re-run the screenshot test to verify the new perspective floor, player cast shadow, and obstacle depth-scale all appear as specified.
